title: In-situ Observation of Secondary Grain Boundary Dislocation and Grain Boundary Disconnection Interaction
content: Grain boundaries (GBs), as two-dimensional defects in crystalline materials, play a crucial role in tailoring structural properties [1]. Extensive experimental [2] and computational [3] studies have explored their structure and kinetics. Among various GB properties, mobility is one of the most critical, as it determines GB dynamics and, consequently, governs microstructural evolution [4]. Disconnection theory provides a valuable framework for investigating this property in greater depth. In this theory, disconnections are intrinsic line defects within GBs, characterized by both a Burgers vector and a step height, and they serve as carriers of GB motion [5]. While numerous studies have examined the effects of misorientation and temperature on GB dynamics [6,7], a knowledge gap remains regarding the interaction between disconnections and other intrinsic GB defects, such as secondary grain boundary dislocations (SGBDs). To address this, we investigate this phenomenon using in-situ heating scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) on a specific type of GB with varying SGBD content.
